data.why: The app bundles its own curated EnvGeo/Around-Japan/Global reference datasets (dataset/*.xlsx) that load automatically at startup, so no seeding is needed; a small CSV with standard column names (Longitude_degE, Latitude_degN, Depth_m, Temperature_degC, Salinity, d18O, dD, d-excess) is written for the browser to upload via the 'Uploaded data' / Quick Visualizer controls, including a missing depth, a missing temperature, and a temperature outlier (99.9 degC) that the app's quality checks should flag.

goals: Load the bundled EnvGeo / Around-Japan / Global reference datasets and filter by dataset name and citation/reference
Build a depth profile of delta-18O, delta-D, d-excess, salinity, and temperature for a chosen region
Construct a temperature-salinity (T-S) diagram with approximate sigma0 density contours to identify water masses
Explore salinity-delta18O regression relationships across datasets
Visualize spatial-temporal structure in 3D/4D (longitude, latitude, depth, selected parameter) and on 2D maps
Upload a CSV/XLSX of new measurements, run the quality/missing-value checks and duplicate/overlap screening against bundled reference data, and export filtered results and figures

review.summary: The tree accurately records the core loop (filter, T-S, depth profile, salinity–δ18O regression, upload quality check, duplicate screen), its labels are clean, and the ten screens I opened all support it. It leaves out the spatial half of the tool (maps, 3D/4D in lon/lat/depth, linked selection, vertical sections, the Global source), so it needs those added or flagged before filing.
